correctness.rationale: The path segment disintegration is a conditional measurable bijection to endpoint value plus independent Brownian bridge noise, giving I(full left;full right|X_t)=I(Y0;Y1|X_t). Exact Gaussian posterior precision has offdiag 1-c/delta and diagonal b/delta+(1-t)/t, a/delta+t/(1-t); the mutual-information expression follows with 0<=rho^2<1. AM-GM uniquely maximizes at sqrt(a)/(sqrt(a)+sqrt(b)) unless delta=c. Rank-one nonzero endpoint coupling gives a singular conditional joint supported on a line versus a diffuse conditional product; pinned degeneracies give zero. The KL chain rule establishes the single-cut factorization projection. A standalone 10,704-assertion exact-rational checker corroborates but does not replace these universal proof steps. No unproved numerical extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: A natural full-path conditional information/KL invariant quantifies how strongly a Brownian endpoint boundary coupling violates Markov splitting, refines the known qualitative Markov criterion to a complete zero/finite/infinite information classification, and identifies the unique most informative cut independently of endpoint cross-covariance. This optimum gives a structural rule for where a one-point observation exposes most residual two-sided dependence; singular boundary behavior is genuinely discontinuous in KL. The result is intrinsically motivated by nonlocal Brownian boundaries and cannot be obtained merely by renaming a finite table entry.
